title: Tribal Movements Tana Bhagat Movement
definition: The Tana Bhagat Movement was a socio-religious and political tribal uprising (1914) led by the Oraon tribe in the Chota Nagpur region, characterized by a synthesis of Sanskritization, monotheism, and anti-colonial nationalism.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the transition of tribal movements from localized agrarian resistance to integration with the mainstream Indian National Movement (INC).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Tribal Movements Tana Bhagat Movement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Understanding of British Land Revenue Systems (Zamindari/Ryotwari)
Basic knowledge of Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act (CNT Act)
